To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reliability and lifetime of highly aligned SWCNT lines can be predicted by a simple, empirical test and that, for well-fabricated networks, electromigration appears to be the dominant degradation mechanism.

the reliability of SWCNT networks is highly sensitive to the initial electrical resistance of the network, that the reliability of these networks can be modeled as an electromigration process, and that this reliability model can be used to predict the failure of the network.
highly aligned, network-based SWCNT lines can be fabricated with low resistance, high yield, and high reliability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of highly aligned, metallic/semiconductor SWCNTs and how it compares to that of traditional interconnects.
the reliability of highly aligned single-wall carbon nanotube lines, which are a potential interconnect for future nanoelectronic systems.
the development of test methods and analysis tools to understand the electrical reliability of SWCNT networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SWCNT networks can be used in applications where a low current density is required for a long period of time.

the electrical reliability of SWCNT networks is strongly dependent on the initial fabrication process, and that the degradation mechanisms in SWCNT networks are not well-understood, but that the reliability of SWCNTs is comparable to or better than other nanoscale conductors.
the SWCNT lines can withstand DC current density as large as 10 MA cm-2 for several hours, and in some cases, even days, but that this performance is strongly dependent upon fabrication quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electrical reliability of highly aligned, metallic SWCNT networks can be significantly improved through a careful fabrication process, and that such networks can withstand DC stressing at high current densities for extended periods of time.
the electrical reliability of SWCNT networks can be greatly improved by optimizing fabrication and test methods.
the reliability of highly aligned SWCNTs is highly dependent on the quality of fabrication, but can be comparable to the reliability of state-of-the-art copper interconnects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability of these SWCNT networks is strongly dependent upon fabrication quality, which is an important consideration when designing nanoelectronic devices.

, despite the fact that SWCNTs have a high intrinsic resistance, they can be used to fabricate nanoscale electrical interconnects that can be subjected to large DC current densities and still retain their electrical properties.
SWCNT networks can be used as highly reliable interconnects in nanoelectronics applications.
